text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Fifteen European countries are committed to finding a compromise that would allow France to sign a stability pact next week. The new government had said it needed time to study the agreement, designed to keep public deficits under control for countries joining a single European currency, and had called for more emphasis on fighting unemployment.
-- Generale des Eaux chairman Jean-Marie Messier confirms forecast for a 1997 profit of more than five billion francs.
-- La Poste considers selling casualty insurance products in its network of 17,000 post offices, possibly in partnership with insurer AGF.
-- Air Littoral to sign co-operation agreement with Lufthansa.

-- U.S.-based Armstrong World Industries files court action to block Sommer Allibert from merging its floor covering business, including Domco Inc, with Tarkett AG. Chairman George Lorch says in an interview that Sommer Allibert is not respecting Domco's minority shareholders.
-- Automobiles Peugeot confirms plan to cut 2,816 jobs in France.
-- Workers at Renault Vilvoorde plant call for strike after appointment of an independent expert to review alternative solutions to shutdown.
-- Paris court cancels waiver given to Lagardere on bid requirement for Filipacchi Media shares.
-- Terms of a compromise on European stability pact to be detailed in the coming days.
-- European Commission President Jacques Santer meets Prime Minister Lionel Jospin and President Jacques Chirac today to seek a compromise on France's position on the stability pact.
-- Prime Minister Jospin expected to hold a conference on employment in September, according to FO union.
-- Prime Minister's office is studying the minimum wage SMIC.
